text:
Sara - CSE: hey team — escalating an Acme production issue. Their traffic started hitting function-calling schema validation errors yesterday after we updated the function docs. They report ~15% of requests failing with 422 schema_error. Logs attached below.

Lisa - Support: copying the thread from the customer — they say the model returns an `answer` field but our tool schema expects `result`. They tried to pin the model but failures continue. Billing spike noticed because client retried 5x. :grimacing:

Sara - CSE: repro steps from Acme (they gave this):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\n    "model": "gptx-2",\n    "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a tool integrator. Return only JSON matching the function schema."},{"role":"user","content":"Call the payment_status tool"}],\n    "tool_call": {\n      "name": "payment_status",\n      "arguments_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"transaction_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["transaction_id"]}\n    }\n  }'\n```

Sara - CSE: Acme's logs show we returned model output:```{
  "tool": "payment_status",
  "arguments": {"transaction_id": "abc123"},
  "answer": {"status":"settled","amount":100} 
}``` but the server validator tried to parse `arguments` against the tool schema and then expected the tool runner to return a top-level `result` key. Validation failed because of `answer` vs `result`.

Mike - EngInfra: hmm. A couple of things to clarify: did they pass `tool_result_schema` anywhere? We only treat `tool_call.arguments_schema` as input validation. The runner returns whatever model emits. We convert model outputs into canonical tool-run outputs when the model uses `function_call` format, but apparently this came from a freeform JSON in the model text.

Juan - Eng-ML: likely schema drift caused by a few-shot/example or system prompt. If the system prompt or few-shot examples in their prompt show `answer` instead of `result`, the model will follow that. Also possible that our updated tool docs changed the expected server-side shape and the customer's prompts still show the old shape.

Dylan - ProdEng: can we reproduce internally? Sara, can you drop the exact full prompt they used (including any few-shot examples) and the model version? We need minimal repro to test two potential mitigations: 1) server-side tolerant parser that accepts `answer` and maps to `result`; 2) prompt sanitization to rewrite old-example keys before sending to model.

Sara - CSE: pasted below (redacted user PII):
"system: You are the payment assistant. Always return a JSON object: {\n  \"tool\": \"payment_status\",\n  \"arguments\": {\"transaction_id\": \"<id>\"},\n  \"answer\": {\"status\": \"pending\", \"amount\": 0}\n}\n\nuser: example 1 -> returns above\nuser: real request -> call payment_status with transaction_id abc123"

Mike - EngInfra: got it. So the system prompt explicitly instructs `answer`. That explains it. But why did this only surface after our function docs update? My guess: previously our parser tolerated `answer` and mapped it to `result` at the router level; a recent change tightened validation in the tool-runner (cherry-picked security fix). Patch note: commit 9f3c tightened strict schema enforcement to prevent arbitrary keys.

Juan - Eng-ML: from ML side, models strongly mimic the exact JSON shape shown in system/few-shot. Even when using `function_call` structured API, if the system prompt includes example outputs in text, the model might prefer that. If they used older few-shot examples, that will cause schema drift.

Lisa - Support: customer is asking for immediate workaround. They can't remove the few-shot on their side quickly. Any short-term fix we can deploy?

Dylan - ProdEng: short-term I'd propose two steps: 1) ingest mapping layer in the tool-runner to accept alternate synonyms for result keys (`answer`, `response`, `payload`) and map them to canonical `result`. This can be a hotfix behind a feature flag. 2) roll back the strict validator for affected orgs while we notify them to update prompts. Need to evaluate risk.

Mike - EngInfra: agree. I can put a small tolerant-mapper in the input pipeline. It would be a 25-line change: if model output is JSON and missing `result` but has `answer`, map `result = answer` before validation. Add telemetry flagging. I'll open a PR and flag for emergency deploy.

Juan - Eng-ML: also recommend we add a model-side guard: when `tool_call` present, set `system` content to include explicit schema and say `DO NOT USE examples' top-level keys — use exactly: \"result\"` — but that's brittle. Better: recommend customers update few-shot to match tool docs and add tests in our customer-facing examples.

Sara - CSE: customer also reported that retries caused billing; can we credit them for the failed calls? Finance will need a ticket. Lisa, can you start a credit request with usage logs? We should also notify them about the planned hotfix timeline.

Lisa - Support: will open a billing ticket now and add the usage window 2026-02-15 03:00 - 05:00 UTC. Also will send the customer the workaround: set a post-processing step to rename `answer`->`result` if they control the runner, and suggest removing the few-shot or updating it.

deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline: hotfix branch `hotfix/tool-mapper-2026-02` created by Mike. CI: tests 12/12 passing. Staging deploy starts in 5m, ETA to prod ~30m if no rollback.

Dylan - ProdEng: thanks. Next steps: Mike to push hotfix and add telemetry for `mismatched_schema_key` event; Juan to add a guidance blurb in docs and reach out to a few high-usage customers who use function calling; Sara/Lisa to coordinate communication and billing credit.

Sara - CSE: noted. Please keep me posted in-thread. Acme is on standby for the staging URL to validate.

Mike - EngInfra: staging up: https://staging-runner.redwood.example/health — hotfix deployed. Sara, can you send Acme the staging endpoint and ask them to retry one failing request?

Sara - CSE: pinged Acme with staging URL and repro curl. They confirmed one failing request succeeded and no schema_error. They also confirmed retries dropped and no additional cost. Customer is happy with temporary fix.

Lisa - Support: closing loop — billing ticket filed (BT-1192). Will follow up after postmortem.

Juan - Eng-ML: will add a brief internal note to docs about prompt examples causing schema drift. Also we'll add an e2e test that includes a few-shot with alternate key names to ensure pipeline mapping remains robust.

Dylan - ProdEng: leaving action items: Mike PR -> merge/monitor, Juan doc + e2e, Sara/Lisa billing + customer comms. Good catch. :shipit:

Sara - CSE: thanks all. Closing thread once PR is in prod and we have postmortem summary.
